setup: CREATE TABLE new_customers (customer_id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, country VARCHAR, segment VARCHAR, signed_up DATE)

job: price_changes holds new list prices for some products. Give each of those products its new price, and leave every other product as it is.
setup: CREATE TABLE price_changes (product_id INTEGER, list_price DECIMAL(10,2))
sql: UPDATE products SET list_price = c.list_price FROM price_changes c WHERE c.product_id = products.product_id

job: product_feed is the supplier's latest list. Bring products up to date from it: a product already in products takes the feed's name, category and list price, and a product not yet in products is added, not discontinued. Products the feed doesn't mention stay as they are.
setup: CREATE TABLE product_feed (product_id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, list_price DECIMAL(10,2))

INSERT INTO product_feed VALUES (1, 'Books item 01, second edition', 'books', 149.00), (2, 'Games item 02', 'games', 160.00), (9, 'Music item 09', 'music', 21.40), (61, 'Garden item 61', 'garden', 35.00), (62, 'Toys item 62', 'toys', 12.50)
sql: UPDATE products SET name = f.name, category = f.category, list_price = f.list_price FROM product_feed f WHERE f.product_id = products.product_id
INSERT INTO products SELECT product_id, name, category, list_price, false FROM product_feed f WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM products p WHERE p.product_id = f.product_id)

job: Create a view named store_revenue with a row for each store that has delivered orders: the store's id and the revenue of its delivered orders. Web orders, which have no store, are left out.
evidence: A line's revenue is its quantity times its unit price times (1 - its discount).
sql: CREATE VIEW store_revenue AS SELECT o.store_id, sum(i.quantity * i.unit_price * (1 - i.discount)) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' AND o.store_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.store_id

job: Make daily_orders, which gives each day and the number of orders placed that day. New orders keep arriving, and daily_orders must always be up to date without anyone refreshing it.
sql: CREATE VIEW daily_orders AS SELECT CAST(ordered_at AS DATE) AS day, count(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY CAST(ordered_at AS DATE)

job: The returns from 1 December 2025 on were loaded twice by mistake. Remove the extra copies, so that each of those returns is there once.
setup: INSERT INTO returns SELECT * FROM returns WHERE returned_on >= DATE '2025-12-01'
sql: CREATE TABLE returns_once AS SELECT DISTINCT * FROM returns WHERE returned_on >= DATE '2025-12-01'
DELETE FROM returns WHERE returned_on >= DATE '2025-12-01'
INSERT INTO returns SELECT * FROM returns_once
DROP TABLE returns_once

job: Move every cancelled order placed before 1 July 2025, with its order lines, out of orders and order_items into two new tables, orders_archive and order_items_archive, with the same columns.
sql: CREATE TABLE orders_archive AS SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00'
CREATE TABLE order_items_archive AS SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM orders_archive)
DELETE FROM order_items WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM orders_archive)
DELETE FROM orders WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM orders_archive)

job: Add a column order_total to orders that holds each order's revenue.
evidence: A line's revenue is its quantity times its unit price times (1 - its discount).
sql: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN order_total DECIMAL(12,4)
UPDATE orders SET order_total = (SELECT sum(i.quantity * i.unit_price * (1 - i.discount)) FROM order_items i WHERE i.order_id = orders.order_id)

job: Some customers' emails have capital letters, or spaces around them. Make every email lower case with no spaces around it, and leave missing emails missing.
setup: UPDATE customers SET email = upper(email) WHERE customer_id % 7 = 0 AND email IS NOT NULL
UPDATE customers SET email = '  ' || email || ' ' WHERE customer_id % 11 = 0 AND email IS NOT NULL
sql: UPDATE customers SET email = lower(trim(email)) WHERE email IS NOT NULL

sql: UPDATE products SET list_price = list_price / 10 WHERE category = 'toys'

job: Create a table loyalty with each customer who has at least one delivered order and the points they earned: one point for each whole 10 of revenue across their delivered orders.
evidence: A line's revenue is its quantity times its unit price times (1 - its discount).
sql: CREATE TABLE loyalty AS SELECT o.customer_id, floor(sum(i.quantity * i.unit_price * (1 - i.discount)) / 10) AS points FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id

sql: DELETE FROM products WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)
